title: Pavel Durov: running Telegram with a tiny team via contests, solo builders and fast shipping
summary: A collection of Durov's Telegram channel posts (2018-2026) on how Telegram hires through public coding contests, ships fast with a small team, rewrites core products, and argues new apps can win by copying only what works. Also covers solo-built mini apps, data portability and the cost of platform gatekeepers.

principles.text: Hire through open contests: winning a public coding contest is the only way onto the engineering team.
principles.quote: Telegram contests offer generous prize money — and the only path to joining our engineering team.

principles.text: Run a competition for everything you build; winners get prize money and a chance to join the dev team.
principles.quote: Eventually there’ll be a competition for everything we do (Android, C++, voice calls etc). Winners get mighty prizes and a chance to join our dev team.

principles.text: Competition drives progress, so pay generously for top talent to compete in public.
Enter a crowded market by borrowing only what works from predecessors, then innovate and differentiate elsewhere.
principles.quote: MemHash proved there’s always room for a new app on Telegram — provided you deeply understand which features made its predecessors popular. The key is to borrow only what works while innovating and differentiating elsewhere

principles.text: Grow a product by continuously listening to users and shipping many useful features over years.
principles.quote: Then, by continuously listening to users and innovating, we introduced hundreds of new useful features over 12 years.

principles.text: One person with a strong concept and minimalist design can build a viral, revenue-generating product in days without a team or marketing budget.
principles.quote: Without a team or marketing budget, he single-handedly implemented everything — design, concept, client-side code, and server-side code.
